profile.headline: [[ Staff Software Engineer and Tech Mentor | Rust Trainer & Innovation Hacker | Motorcycle Racer ]] at DITTO
profile.summary:
I architect and deliver high-performance systems that solve impossible technical challenges at scale. At Pluto TV (Paramount Streaming), I lead cross-platform development initiatives serving millions of daily viewers across web, mobile, and connected TV platforms.

Recent impact:

- Ported Data Analytics Hub to Rust cross-platform library with native bindings (C/iOS-Swift, Java-Kotlin/Android), unifying analytics across streaming platforms and consolidating multiple apps/repos
- Pioneered embedded Linux optimization achieving up to 85% performance improvement (<2s load time on resource-constrained devices), protecting >$1M monthly revenue and enabling critical partnership retention & expansion
- Evangelized Rust adoption within React/TypeScript organization through technical mentorship of 10+ engineers and Community of Practice leadership

Technical depth:
Deep expertise in systems programming (Rust, C), cross-platform architecture, and performance optimization for resource-constrained environments. Proven track record of making strategic technology decisions that balance innovation with pragmatic delivery—from building spatial navigation systems for smart TVs (32bit & 64bit arch), Set Top Boxes (highly constrained) and Game Consoles (artificially limited) to architecting analytics SDKs deployed across iOS, Android, and web platforms.

Leadership approach:
I create opportunities for engineering teams to exceed their potential by challenging boundaries and bringing unexpected approaches to complex problems. Whether mentoring engineers new to systems programming or establishing CI/CD pipelines for cross-platform compilation, I focus on empowering teams to deliver impossible outcomes at warp speed.

Beyond the code:
Third Place finisher on Paramount/PlutoTV's 2024 Advent of Code internal leaderboard. Recognized with the 2022 Fauncey Award for exemplifying company values through breakthrough performance optimization. Active in the Rust community and passionate about motorcycle racing—both require precision, calculated risk-taking, and unwavering focus.

Currently Staff Software Engineer at Ditto, building SDKs for real-time peer-to-peer sync across web, mobile, and native platforms.

projects.title: RustConf 2026 Workshop: Using Advent of Code as an FFI Playground
projects.description:
Using Advent of Code (AoC) puzzles as the substrate, participants build a working Rust FFI library from scratch, wrapping a real AoC solution in a C glue layer and calling it from multiple different target languages. By the end of the workshop, attendees leave with a working multi-language project, a replicable methodology, and hands-on intuition for the pitfalls that make production FFI hard.
AoC problems are uniquely well-suited for FFI practice because they have diverse input/output types (primitives, strings, iterators), a motivating narrative that makes repetition feel worthwhile, no production baggage — you can break things freely — and progressively increasing complexity across 12-25 days of problems each year. Unlike algorithm-focused competitive programming, this approach uses AoC’s rich problem variety to stress-test real cross-platform FFI patterns: string encoding mismatches between Java and Swift, and the lowest-common-denominator constraints that make production FFI viable.

https://rustconf2026.sched.com/event/2IEzd

projects.title: Ditto x Cactus
projects.description:
Two phones, no internet, one shared brain. DittoXCactus is an offline-first RAG system: devices merge a distributed vector index as a grow-only CRDT over BLE/Wi-Fi (Ditto mesh sync) and answer queries with the WAN off — on-device Qwen models (Cactus / llama.cpp) handle both embedding and flashcard generation.

The hard problems were reliability, not plumbing: I built a cross-platform embedding-determinism harness with locked baselines that gates iOS↔Android reproducibility of inference output, and hardened a six-gate retrieval-to-generation pipeline where each gate absorbs a documented on-device small-model failure mode — reasoning leaks, grounding failures, duplicate generation.
